new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the first syllable in citation forms (a word uttered alone); in connected speech prominence is on the first syllable of each breath group, stronger on emphasised breath groups; the system is said to be the same as in the Manbhum dialect of Bengali (MD). No contrastive function is claimed.
new_statements.exceptions: None visible in the snippet (passage truncated after the breath-group example).
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly citation-form/word domain ('when the word is uttered alone') versus breath-group-initial stress in connected speech; 'MD' = Manbhum Dialect of Bengali per the volume's abbreviations page ('KT. = Kharia Thar; MD. = Manbhum Dialect of [Bengali]').
new_statements.identity_note: Dasgupta 1978 describes 'Kharia Thar', the Bengali-based speech of the Hill Kharias of Manbhum (Purulia district, West Bengal, and adjoining Singhbhum), i.e. exactly Glottolog khar1283 / ISO ksy; he treats it as a dialect distinct from the Manbhum (Jharkhandi) dialect of Bengali (p. 95) but states its stress and intonation are the same as that dialect's. Not to be confused with Munda Kharia (khar1287) or with the Munda 'Lodha' of Midnapore described in LSI-West Bengal 2016. The Malpaharia initial-stress statement in LSI-Jharkhand concerns the sister variety malp1246, not this language.
